# KidMindPath — full reference

Site: https://www.kidmindpath.com/
Language of the site: Latvian. An English summary lives at https://www.kidmindpath.com/en/
Last updated: 2026-09-03


## What it is

KidMindPath is a free collection of five educational browser games for young
children, roughly ages 2 to 7, in the Latvian language. It is an independent,
non-commercial project — not a company, not a subscription, not a storefront.

The games open directly in a web browser. Nothing is downloaded, nothing is
installed, no app store is involved, and no account is created. Any modern
browser on a phone, tablet or computer will run them.


## What it costs

Nothing. All five games are entirely free. There are no in-app purchases, no
paid tier, no "premium" version, and no free trial that ends. There is no
payment mechanism on the site at all.


## Advertising

There is none, in any of the five games or on any page of the site. The site is
not connected to any ad network.

This is enforced technically, not just promised. Every page carries a strict
Content-Security-Policy (`default-src 'self'`) that forbids loading anything
from a third-party origin — scripts, styles, images, fonts, or network
connections. An ad script could not run here even if someone added one.


## Privacy and data

- No analytics of any kind. No Google Analytics, no tracking pixels, no
  third-party scripts.
- No account, no registration, no email address, no login.
- No cookies used for tracking.
- Every file the site serves, including its webfonts, comes from its own
  domain. The pages make no third-party requests.
- A child's progress — stars, collected cards, finished tasks — is written to
  the browser's own storage (localStorage and IndexedDB) on that device. It is
  never transmitted, because there is no server that could receive it. The site
  is static files on GitHub Pages.
- Entering a child's first name and age on the home page is optional. When
  entered, it is stored locally on the device and used only to order the game
  cards and show progress in one place.
- A parent can delete all stored progress across all five games with a single
  button, on the "Vecākiem" (for parents) page.

Full policy, including a dedicated children's-privacy section:
https://www.kidmindpath.com/privatums.html


## The five games

Age ranges are guidance, not gates: every game is open to every child
regardless of the age entered on the home page.

1. Little Fingers Paint — https://www.kidmindpath.com/Paint/
   Ages 2-7. Builds creativity and fine motor skills.
   Finger painting with brushes, colours, stickers and colouring pages.
   Latvian. Works offline after the first visit.

2. Mācāmies angliski! ("Let's learn English") — https://www.kidmindpath.com/ENG-learning/
   Ages 2-7. Builds English vocabulary, at two difficulty levels.
   For Latvian-speaking children; the interface is Latvian, the taught
   vocabulary is English. Works offline after the first visit.

3. Ciparu dārzs ("Number garden") — https://www.kidmindpath.com/Memory/
   Ages 2-6. Builds memory and early maths.
   Five small memory and counting games. Latvian. Works offline after the
   first visit.

4. Prāta piedzīvojumu sala ("Mind adventure island") — https://www.kidmindpath.com/PrataSala/
   Ages 4-7. Builds attention, memory and problem solving.
   A mini-game adventure. Latvian. This is the one game that needs an internet
   connection each time it is opened; it does not cache itself for offline use.

5. Burtu Feja ("Letter fairy") — https://www.kidmindpath.com/KidlaTest/
   Ages 5-6. Builds knowledge of the Latvian alphabet and early reading.
   Latvian. Works offline after the first visit.

Several children can share one device: the home page holds multiple profiles
with different names and ages, and counts progress separately for each. All of
it stays on that device and in that browser.


## Text-to-speech pronunciation

Several games read Latvian text aloud using the device's own text-to-speech
engine, not a voice bundled with the site. Whether Latvian sounds correct
therefore depends on the device: its operating system, its installed TTS
engine, which languages and voices are installed, the browser, and the
manufacturer. The same game can sound correct on one phone and carry a foreign
accent on another.

Step-by-step fixes for Android (including Samsung, Xiaomi/Redmi and Huawei),
iPhone and iPad: https://www.kidmindpath.com/palidziba.html

The short version on Android: update the text-to-speech engine, select
"Speech Recognition & Synthesis from Google" as the preferred engine, add
Latvian to the device's language list, set Latvian as the TTS language, then
fully close and reopen the app. On iPhone/iPad: Settings → General → Language &
Region → Add Latvian, then check Accessibility → Spoken Content → Voices, and
reopen Safari. Some iOS versions simply do not offer a Latvian voice, and that
cannot be worked around by the user.


## Why it exists

Most free games for children make money through advertising or data collection.
That means interruptions unsuited to a small child, and profiling unsuited to
anyone. KidMindPath is an attempt to show that an educational game can be
genuinely free without either: a clear purpose for each game, child-friendly
design with large touch targets, and no server collecting anything on the
child's behalf.
